references.text: The Lord called to Moses from the mountain, just as he now calls to Moses from the tent of meeting.
God promised to meet with Moses and speak to him from the mercy seat between the cherubim, which were located in the tent of meeting.
The pillar of cloud descended at the entrance of the tent when the Lord spoke with Moses, confirming God's communication from the tent of meeting.
The glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle, and Moses could not enter. This explains why the Lord now calls to Moses from the tent of meeting.
The Lord spoke to Moses in the tent of meeting, the same place and in the same manner as in Leviticus 1:1.
Moses heard the voice speaking to him from the mercy seat in the tent of meeting, confirming the location of God's revelation.
The Lord suddenly called to Moses, Aaron, and Miriam and told them to come to the tent of meeting, using the same manner of calling as in Leviticus 1:1.
In the past, God spoke to our ancestors through the prophets, including Moses, but now he has spoken to us through his Son.
Exodus 40:1 establishes the tabernacle as God's dwelling place, making possible the speech from the tent that begins Leviticus.
